summary: Build practical fish farming management skills, improve farm profitability, and plan production with confidence. Enroll in aquaculture business training.
lede: Aquaculture business management connects fish-farm production decisions with operating costs and sales. For farm owners, managers, hatchery technicians, and fish-health staff, it covers assessing sites and planning layouts, managing stocking and monitoring water, feed, and fish health, and using farm records to support budgeting and market planning.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who manage, support, or advise aquaculture operations and need practical control over production, health, feeding, and profitability.
prerequisites: Recommended prerequisites include basic numeracy, comfort with farm records, and a working familiarity with aquaculture or livestock operations. No coding is required. Participants should bring a calculator or laptop for farm budgeting exercises, and a willingness to work through pond logs, feed records, and production planning templates. Experience at beginner to early-intermediate level is appropriate, although the course also supports supervisors who need a more structured approach to farm management.
